ai.description: This lizard reaches 55 cm, including a long, slender tail. It is typically bright green with a prominent, spiny crest along the neck and back. A dark patch often appears behind the eye.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Bronchocela cristatella* is best distinguished by its lack of a distinct tympanum and the presence of a prominent, high-crested ridge of elongated scales along its neck.
ai.habitat: The Green Crested Lizard inhabits lowland tropical rainforests, forest edges, and disturbed areas, typically residing in trees or shrubs below 1,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Green Crested Lizard is primarily diurnal and often exhibits a striking defensive strategy by rapidly shifting its skin color to dark brown when threatened or stressed.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Bronchocela cristatella* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 2–9 eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, often between May and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Bronchocela cristatella* is not native to the Indian subcontinent; it is restricted to Southeast Asia, ranging from the Malay Peninsula to the Indonesian archipelago.
